one_liner: Senior Pentagon analyst overseeing DoD maritime munitions acquisition programs: cost, schedule, risk, budget reviews, and congressional/GAO responses.
fit_summary: This role requires a year of GS-13-equivalent experience directing acquisition oversight for major defense or weapons programs, plus SCI clearance eligibility. Daniel's emergency-management consulting and policy knowledge help with the congressional and legislative-review duties, but nothing on file shows defense acquisition or weapons-program experience. The posting will reject applicants who do not clearly document all three specialized experience elements.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens) under Direct Hire Authority; no federal status needed, but veterans' preference is applied as a positive factor.

One year of specialized experience equivalent to GS-13 covering: end-to-end acquisition oversight of a major defense portfolio, weapons systems, or critical technology programs; evaluating acquisition strategies, baselines, and milestone documentation; and leading cross-functional teams across military service staffs and oversight bodies.
Must be able to obtain and keep a Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) clearance.
Education cannot substitute for experience, and qualifications must be met by the November 4, 2026 closing date.
Resume limited to two pages, with months and hours per week listed for each job.
strategy: Before applying, honestly check whether any IEM work involved federal acquisition, contract or program oversight, cost/schedule tracking, or DoD clients; if none did, treat this as a stretch and put more effort into better-matched roles.

If you supported FEMA or DoD programs at IEM, describe them in acquisition terms: program baselines, cost and schedule risk, milestone reviews, and coordination with agency leadership and oversight bodies.
Lead with legislative work you can document, such as tracking appropriations or authorization language, preparing responses to audits (GAO/OIG), or drafting congressional or oversight materials.
Within the two-page limit, address each of the three specialized-experience elements explicitly, with dates and hours per week, because HR screens only for minimum qualifications.
The application window is only six days (Oct 30–Nov 4, 2026), so finish the resume beforehand and apply early. This is a standing public notice, so you can reapply once you have stronger experience.
Consider entry points that fit you better, such as lower-band AcqDemo or GS-11/12 program analyst roles, FEMA, or DoD legislative affairs positions.
resume_bullets: Supported [client agency] [program name] valued at [$X], tracking cost, schedule, and performance against [baseline/milestones] and flagging [type of risks] to [leadership level].
Analyzed [federal legislation/appropriations provisions] affecting [program area] and prepared [briefings/options papers] for [client officials].
Coordinated [number] cross-functional stakeholders from [agencies/offices] to [outcome], [X] hours/week, [month/year]–[month/year].
interview_questions: Describe a time you identified an unrealistic cost or schedule estimate on a program, and what you recommended.
How would you review the NDAA and appropriations acts for provisions affecting a munitions portfolio?
How do you get military service staff to comply with OSD guidance when you have no direct authority over them?
Walk us through how you would prepare a DoD response to a GAO finding.
watch_outs: The specialized experience requires defense acquisition or weapons-program oversight, which Daniel's known background does not show; the resume may be screened out as not qualified.
SCI clearance is required, and the investigation is lengthy.
The position is on-site at the Pentagon with no telework, which means a daily commute from Manassas.
The six-day open window is very short.
